chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Abu Ja'far, from 'Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Ash'ari, who said:

One of our companions wrote to Abu Ja'far al-Thani عليه السلام: “Inform me about khums: is it due on all that a man gains, whether little or much, from all kinds [of earnings], and also upon craftsmen? So how is that?” He wrote in his own hand: “Khums is after expenses.”

key_terms.الضُّرُوبِ: various kinds or categories of earnings
key_terms.الْخُمُسِ: khums, the one-fifth due on qualifying gains

ai.seo_question: Is khums due on all earnings, and is it calculated before or after expenses?
ai.summary: This hadith records a written question to Imam Abu Ja'far al-Thani عليه السلام concerning whether khums applies to all forms of gain, including small and large amounts and the earnings of craftsmen. The Imam’s written reply establishes the legal principle that khums is due after deducting expenses.
